topic_tag: a state report on removing a river dam
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: In her history of the river, one journalist wrote that the report had ______ the debate over the dam.

worlds.passage: In 1974 a state commission published a report on the last dam on the river, which had stood for sixty years. No legislator, newspaper, or fishing club had ever proposed removing it, and the commission had been asked only to price repairs. Its final chapter went further and recommended taking the dam down. Within a year the legislature had held its first hearings on the dam since it was built, and the state's papers had printed hundreds of letters on both sides of removal. In her history of the river, one journalist wrote that the report had ______ the debate over the dam.
worlds.explanation: No one had proposed removal before the report recommended it, and the first hearings and letters followed, so the report "launched" the debate. "Jolted" fails because there was no existing, stalled debate to shake; "legitimized" fails because no one had held the position the report raised, so there was no dismissed view to give standing to; "muddied" fails because the report made a single clear recommendation.

jolted.why: a debate can be jolted only if it already exists; before the report there was none

legitimized.why: removal was not a fringe view awaiting respect; no one held it until the report raised it

muddied.why: the report gave one plain recommendation, which clarifies rather than confuses

worlds.passage: In 1974 a state commission published a report on the last dam on the river, which had stood for sixty years. Removal had been before the legislature for a decade, backed by the governor and opposed by the power company, and each year the vote was put off while both sides waited for firmer cost figures. The report supplied them, putting removal at a third of the cost of repairs, and within three months the legislature voted. In her history of the river, one journalist wrote that the report had ______ the debate over the dam.
worlds.explanation: A decade-old debate stalled by repeated postponement moved to a vote within months of the report, so the report "jolted" it. "Launched" fails because the debate had been before the legislature for ten years; "legitimized" fails because removal already had the governor's backing and needed no added standing; "muddied" fails because the report gave the clear figures both sides had been waiting for.

launched.quote: before the legislature for a decade
launched.why: the debate began long before the report

legitimized.why: removal was already a mainstream position, so the report did not give it standing

muddied.quote: putting removal at a third of the cost
muddied.why: the report settled the cost question that had stalled the vote rather than confusing it

worlds.passage: In 1974 a state commission published a report on the last dam on the river, which had stood for sixty years. For a decade a small anglers' club had argued for removal against the power company at county meetings, while the state's papers seldom printed its letters and legislators declined to hear its speakers. The commission, chaired by a retired judge, found removal both affordable and lawful. The county meetings went on each spring much as before, and over the next decade editors and legislators began appearing among their speakers. In her history of the river, one journalist wrote that the report had ______ the debate over the dam.
worlds.explanation: The same debate continued at the same pace, but people who had ignored the anglers' side now took part in it after a respected commission found removal workable, so the report "legitimized" the debate. "Launched" fails because the anglers and the power company had been arguing the question for a decade; "jolted" fails because the meetings went on much as before and the change came slowly over the next decade, not as a sudden shock; "muddied" fails because the commission reached a clear finding.

launched.quote: had argued for removal against the power company
launched.why: the two sides were already arguing before the report, so it did not begin the debate

jolted.quote: went on each spring much as before
jolted.why: the debate kept its old rhythm; what changed slowly was who took part, not its pace

muddied.quote: found removal both affordable and lawful
muddied.why: a clear finding makes the question plainer, not murkier

worlds.passage: In 1974 a state commission published a report on the last dam on the river, which had stood for sixty years. Removal had been argued for a decade, with both sides citing a single engineering estimate of its cost. The commission offered three new estimates that differed tenfold and two incompatible counts of the salmon the river could support. Afterward each side quoted in the state's papers whichever figure suited it, and the legislature put off its scheduled vote until a fourth estimate could be made. In her history of the river, one journalist wrote that the report had ______ the debate over the dam.
worlds.explanation: The report replaced one shared estimate with conflicting figures, each side picked its own, and the legislature could not proceed without yet another estimate, so the report "muddied" the debate. "Launched" fails because removal had been argued for a decade; "legitimized" fails because both sides were already arguing in the open from an official estimate; "jolted" fails because the report led to a postponed vote, not to sudden movement.

launched.quote: Removal had been argued for a decade

legitimized.quote: both sides citing a single engineering estimate
legitimized.why: removal was already argued on equal official terms, so there was no ignored position to raise up

jolted.why: the report slowed the process down instead of shaking it into motion
